objective: Implement the manager-frozen CFR-168 C14-LIVE-A1 pre-effect cleanup contract on exact base 333e410: preserve the exact primary exception outermost, attach the first cleanup fault as its immediate cause while retaining prior effective chains, perform bounded descriptor cleanup without raw-FD retry, prevent _open memory-owner orphaning and 22,912-byte double growth, cover every live direct ancestry/signature/server owner, synchronize source truth, and leave A2/B3 plus sealed/composite successors unchanged.

risk.rationale: An Ultra manager decision has already frozen the cross-owner exception, recovery, FD and ownership contracts into deterministic identity/count/state oracles. The implementation remains cross-cutting in one Python product file and needs a High implementer plus an independent Ultra reviewer. Any new authority, response/wire, persisted, public, or unresolved state-machine choice escalates back to Ultra Freeze rather than being guessed by the implementer.

disallowed_actions: Change _PreparedHTTPMutationResponses, _HTTPMutationResponseSlot, the POST response arm, request-loop finally, response selection or wire publication
Implement C14-LIVE-A2, B3, a global RetryableCleanup shape, secondary-failure wire/log protocol or a new cleanup container
Change AccountedHTTPUploadSealedAncestry, AccountedHTTPUploadSignatureVerificationComposite, AccountedHTTPUploadExistingTerminalOwner or other sealed/composite successor orchestration
Retry a raw file-descriptor integer after close reports an error
Use an unbounded retry, sleep-until-success loop, request hang or process-wide cleanup registry
Clear a scalar, permit, process, child or owner pointer before its release has committed
Replace the exact primary exception object, omit the first cleanup cause or discard the primary's pre-existing effective chain
Change traversal order, signature decisions, verification commands, public error/status behavior, persisted state, resource profiles or serialized formats
Claim that verification-process cleanup rolls back effects already performed by the configured command
Edit the CFR-168 status, current cycle, history, roadmap, Install, Dogfood, Close or Retrospect evidence
Self-review, self-approve, integrate, amend, rebase, squash, merge canonical or reuse an excluded reviewer session
Discard user changes or use destructive Git cleanup

non_goals: Implement A2/B3 post-effect response/wire ownership or make it an A1 acceptance prerequisite
Wire any sealed/composite terminal successor into production
Create a public retry API, persistent cleanup journal, exception wrapper type, ExceptionGroup or global secondary-failure collection
Guarantee recovery from an eternally non-committing ledger release or unreapable process
Retry an ambiguously closed raw FD instead of conservatively abandoning its numeric ownership
Change ancestry result/order, signature policy semantics, verification command selection, deadlines, resource profiles or HTTP responses
Roll back external effects created by configured verification commands
Update Rust, packaging, schemas, devcontainer, dogfood, issue status or lifecycle terminal records
Treat passing tests or one reviewer as canonical integration, Install, Dogfood, CFR-168 Close or global C14 closure

invariants.statement: The exact original operation, construction or validation exception object is outermost; the exact first cleanup fault is its immediate explicit cause.
invariants.falsification_test: Inject distinct primary and cleanup exception objects and assert identity; restoring cleanup-first, wrapping the primary or omitting the cause must fail.

invariants.statement: The cleanup fault's prior effective cause/context chain followed by the primary's prior effective chain remains below the immediate cleanup cause, cycle-free and with each exception identity at most once.
invariants.falsification_test: Seed distinct, shared and cyclic cause/context nodes; deleting, reordering, duplicating or cycling a node must fail the exact identity-sequence oracle.

invariants.statement: Rebuilding the bounded exception chain does not retain raw policy, parsed policy, commit payload, process output or owner frames through release observation.
invariants.falsification_test: Hold only weak references to payload sentinels and inspect release callbacks; retaining a traceback/local through the chain must fail collection and observer assertions.

invariants.statement: The first cleanup fault determines cause or cleanup-only outer identity; later cleanup faults never replace it and create no global container.
invariants.falsification_test: Make three independent cleanup actions fail with distinct objects and require the first identity to remain the only attached cleanup fault while all actions are attempted boundedly.

invariants.statement: A retryable scalar, permit, child, process or memory owner remains published until its own release commits; post-commit exceptions consume ownership exactly once while still propagating.
invariants.falsification_test: Inject pre- and post-commit release faults and assert same-owner retry, before/after ledger current, no double release and no false zero.

invariants.statement: One session close performs a finite sweep of all independent descriptor owners after the first fault, detaching each numeric before one close, releasing logical control, and allowing the bounded wrapper retry to drain the 11,456-byte source reservation.
invariants.falsification_test: Make every descriptor close report a distinct error; an early break, unbounded retry, repeated numeric, residual current or open permit must fail.

invariants.statement: A descriptor number consumed before an ambiguous close result is never retried, even if the same integer is later reused by ambient authority.
invariants.falsification_test: Reuse the failed integer before owner retry and prove the ambient descriptor remains open; restoring numeric retry must close it and fail the oracle.

invariants.statement: _open settles the exact old _memory owner before polling, allocating, acquiring or constructing a replacement; a settlement fault preserves exactly 11,456 retained bytes and never grows to 22,912.
invariants.falsification_test: Hold the constructor error/source, fail old-memory cleanup and reenter _open; restoring overwrite must increase acquire/constructor calls and ledger current to 22,912.

invariants.statement: A1 covers the live direct AccountedHTTPUploadAncestry, AccountedRemoteSignaturePolicyAuthority, AccountedCommitSignaturePolicy, AccountedServerVerification/run_server_verification, commit source and validate_sealed_commit cleanup loci.
invariants.falsification_test: Inject a primary-plus-cleanup fault at each named constructor/body/finally/wrapper surface and require one exact identity/state oracle per route.

invariants.statement: Goal-directed and full-BFS ancestry, signature decisions, verification commands, deadline phases, accounting profiles, error-origin classification and pre-effect durable authority remain otherwise unchanged.
invariants.falsification_test: Run the established focused and adjacent suites plus before/after authority hashes; any changed result/order/profile/status or durable byte blocks acceptance.

invariants.statement: A2/B3 response/wire owners and sealed/composite successor class bodies remain AST-identical to 333e410.
invariants.falsification_test: Compare exact qualified AST bodies against 333e410 and fail if any excluded unit changes, even when the broad suite passes.

invariants.statement: All four canonical source documents and known limitations distinguish live direct ancestry/signature/server owners from unwired sealed/composite successors and state bounded cleanup/FD limitations exactly.
invariants.falsification_test: Restore production-unwired wording for a live owner, omit the conservative FD/process limitation or overclaim persistent primitive recovery and require source/project docs review to fail.
